slot.brief: Find the equation of a line through the intersection of two given lines satisfying an extra condition (parallel/perpendicular to a third line).

stem: Find the equation of the line through the intersection of $x-y=3$ and $2x+y=3$, perpendicular to $x-2y+4=0$.

verdicts.working: Solving the first two equations gives the intersection (2,-1). The line x-2y+4=0 has slope 1/2, so a perpendicular line has slope -2. Through (2,-1): y+1=-2(x-2), or 2x+y-3=0.

working:
$x-y=3,\ 2x+y=3\ \Rightarrow\ (x,y)=(2,-1)$. The given line has slope $\dfrac{1}{2}$, so the required slope is $-2$. $y+1=-2(x-2)\ \Rightarrow\ 2x+y-3=0$.

Independent check: Solving the first two equations gives the intersection (2,-1). The line x-2y+4=0 has slope 1/2, so a perpendicular line has slope -2. Through (2,-1): y+1=-2(x-2), or 2x+y-3=0.
solution:
Solving $x-y=3$ and $2x+y=3$ gives the intersection $(2,-1)$. The given line has slope $\frac12$, so the perpendicular line has slope $-2$.
$$y+1=-2(x-2)\Rightarrow 2x+y-3=0$$
